 Judgment

The claimants have filed this appeal against the Judgment and Award dated 30.05.2016 passed in MVC.No.1152/2015 by the VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2.

sentences.text: Parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The claim petition is based on the following facts: On 12th October 2014, at approximately 19:00 hours, the deceased, Dipesh Dilip Gawade, was riding a motorcycle with registration No.KA-22/EK-0226 (referred to as the offending vehicle) along with Sri Rohan Laxman Gurav as the pillion rider.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10647-DB
They were traveling from Peeranawadi to Kinne.

While on the Peeranawadi-Jamboti road, near Santibastawad cross, the rider of the offending vehicle was operating it at a high speed and in a reckless and negligent manner, without adhering to traffic rules.

sentences.text: As a result, the offending vehicle collided with an oncoming motorcycle with registration No.KA-22/EK-2885, causing a severe accident.
Due to the impact of the collision, the deceased fell onto the road and sustained grievous injuries to vital parts of his body, leading to his immediate demise at the accident site.
The petitioners were dependent on the deceased for their livelihood.
The deceased was a student in the first semester of a diploma program at Jain College and was also employed as a computer operator in private service, earning a monthly income of Rs.8,500/-.
His sudden death has resulted in a loss of financial support for the petitioners.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their son, while petitioner No. 3 has lost her elder brother.

It is claimed that Respondent No. 1, the owner of the offending vehicle, and Respondent No. 2, the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to provide compensation.
Therefore, the claimants request the petition to be allowed.
Upon the service of the notice, Respondent No. 1 was absent and proceeded ex-parte.
Respondent No. 2 appeared through its counsel and submitted objections, refuting all allegations and claims made by the petitioners.
Specifically, they disputed the information regarding the deceased's earnings.
Furthermore, it was argued that there was a violation of the policy conditions by the owner, Respondent No. 1, of the offending vehicle.
This violation pertains to the rider of the offending vehicle not possessing a valid and effective driver's license on the date of the accident.

Therefore, they request the dismissal of the petition against Respondent No. 2.
5.

On the basis of rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Mr. Dipesh Dileep Gawade died due to the injuries sustained in an accident occurred on 12.10.2014 at about 19:00 hours on Peeranwadi-Jamboti Road, near Santibastawad cross, Santibastawad, Belagavi, due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EK-0226 by its rider?
2. Are petitioners entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order?
To prove the case of petitioners, petitioner No.1 was examined as P.W.-1 and got marked Ex.P-1 to 7.

On the respondent side the official of respondent No. 2 was examined as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R-1 to 18.
7.

After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal has given its findings to the above issues as under :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : The petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.8,61,000/- with future interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till complete realization from respondent No.1.

3 Issue No.3 : As per final order.

sentences.text: 8. In view of the above findings, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.8,61,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till its complete realization fastening the liability on respondent No.1.
Being dissatisfied with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal as to the liability of the Insurance Company as well as quantum of compensation

,
claimants have preferred this appeal.
SUBMISSION OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR CLAIMANTS.
Learned counsel for the appellant-claimants submits that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to the law and facts of the case.

The Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on the owner of vehicle on the ground that as on the date of accident as per Ex.P.7-Charge sheet is filed against the rider of the vehicle for the commission of offence under Section 279, 338 and 304A of IPC and Section 3 r/w. Section 181 of MV Act.

The initial burden is on the Insurance Company and company has to establish the breach of policy conditions by cogent evidence, therefore the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside and company is held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, he submits that the a full bench Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., v. Swaran Singh and others, reported in 2004 ACJ 1,
was pleased to held that the company cannot escape from its liability to pay the compensation on the ground that the driver of the vehicle is not having valid license.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the order passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.
Further, he submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

On all these grounds, NC:
2023:KHC-D:10647-DB sought for enhancement of compensation, fastening the liability to pay compensation on the Insurance Company under the principle of pay and recovery.
SUBMISSION ON BEHALF OF INSURANCE COMPANY 10.

As against this, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has submits that the Tribunal has passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts and Tribunal has awarded 9%
interest on the compensation, which is on the higher side that there are no grounds to interfere with the judgment and award as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
On all these grounds, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments on both sides and on perusal of the material on record, the following points would arise for our consideration:
(1) Whether the appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(2) Whether respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation under principle of pay and recovery?

Our answers to the above points are as under :
Point No.1 and 2 partly in the affirmative.
Point No.3 as per the final order

Point Nos.1 and 2:
13.
We have carefully examined the material placed on record.
Upon perusal of the same, it is clear that there is no dispute regarding the accident.
It is also not in dispute that Mr. Dipesh Dilip Gawade, the deceased, died in the road traffic accident.
The involvement of the vehicle is also undisputed.

The second respondent has raised an objection that the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation on the grounds that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident.
This fact is evident from the charge sheet submitted by the Investigating Officer, which is not contested by the claimants.

In this regard, a perusal of the charge sheet makes it crystal clear that, after thorough investigation, the Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offenses under Sections 279, 338, and 304A of the IPC and Section 3, read with Section 181 of the M.V. Act.

The Investigating Officer also submitted a charge sheet against respondent No.2, the owner of the motor vehicle, for the commission of an offense under Section 5,
read with Section 180 of the M.V. Act.
P.W.1-Dilip Krishna Gavade did not mention anything about the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer.
During his cross-examination, he clearly admitted the contents of the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer.
R.W.1-A.Umesh Bhat has clearly stated in his evidence that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid and effective driving license and also provided details about the charge sheet.

The document produced by the respondent- Insurance Company reveals that the Insurance Company took legal steps against respondent No.1,
the owner of the vehicle, to produce the driving license, but the same was not produced by respondent No.1.
Considering this fact, the Tribunal has assigned liability to respondent No. 1, the owner of the vehicle.
14. The Tribunal has failed to adhere to the decision in the case of Swaran Singh (supra).
In light of the said ruling by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the Tribunal should have imposed liability on the Insurance Company based on the principle of pay and recovery.

Consequently, the Insurance Company is - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10647-DB obligated to provide compensation with the liberty to recover the same from respondent No.1, the owner of the vehicle, in accordance with the law.
Regarding the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month, which is not Shri.

sentences.text: According to the chart issued by KSLSA, the notional income for the year 2014 is Rs.7,500/- per month.
The deceased was 20 years old at the time of the accident.
Following the precedent set by the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, an '18' multiplier is applicable.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In accordance with the National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the income needs to be added as future prospects, and 1/3rd should be deducted for the personal and living expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the claimants are entitled to compensation under the loss of dependency category, calculated as follows: (Rs.7,500/- + 40% - 1/3 = Rs.7,000/-) x 12 x 18 = Rs.15,12,000/-.

For the aforementioned reasons and discussions, the claimants are entitled to an enhancement of compensation as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs.15,12,000/-
2 Loss of consortium Rs.1,20,000/-
(3 dependants) 3 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4 For funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/-
transportation of dead body Total Rs.16,62,000/-
16.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in affirmative and point No.2 in partly affirmative.

17. For the above reasons and discussions, we pass the following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed.
(ii) The impugned Judgment and Award dated 30.05.2016 passed in MVC.No.1152/2015 by the VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi is hereby modified.
